newsitem.title: USA: October retail sales post weak rise as new-car sales fall.
newsitem.headline: October retail sales post weak rise as new-car sales fall.

text.p: Sales at retail stores posted a weaker-than-expected gain in October, the Commerce Department said on Thursday, held down by weak business for new-car dealers.
Total retail sales increased a slim 0.2 percent to a seasonally adjusted $206.6 billion after a revised 0.8 percent increase in September sales.
The rise in October sales was lower than the 0.3 percent increase forecast by Wall Street economists.
It represented a lackluster start to the fourth quarter, which traditionally is the peak of the retail sales season because of holiday shopping between Thanksgiving and Christmas.
During October, sales by new-car dealers -- which accounts for roughly a quarter of total retail business -- dropped 0.3 percent to $50.7 billion following a 1.7 percent surge in September.
Excluding cars, retail sales were up 0.4 percent last month after a rising 0.5 percent in September.
Overall sales of durable goods, which includes cars as well as furniture and other long-lasting goods, were flat in October after rising 0.9 percent in September.
All the monthly gain in overall business was in nondurable items like food and gasoline, where sales increased 0.3 percent following a 0.7 percent September rise.
Sales by general merchandise stores rose 0.7 percent in October to $26.1 billion after being flat in September.

A slump in consumer spending was a key reason that national economic growth, measured by gross domestic product, slowed to a 2.2 percent annual rate in the third quarter from 4.7 percent in the second quarter.
Most economists foresee a modest rebound in growth in the closing quarter, fuelled partly by anticipated brisk retail sales during the holiday shopping period.

Steady job growth and a booming stock market have boosted incomes and raised consumer confidence about the economy's direction. Though household debts are high, analysts cite surveys in which consumers say they intend to spend more at Christmas.

On Wednesday the Federal Reserve decided to keep interest rates steady amid signs inflation remains moderate, which removed the potential threat of higher borrowing costs for credit-card balances and loans.
Previously, the department said September sales had risen 0.7 percent but it revised that up slightly to a 0.8 percent increase.

Sales of building materials rose 0.7 percent last month to $11.3 billion after a 0.4 percent rise in September. But furniture sales dropped 1 percent to $11.4 billion in October after a 0.2 percent fall in September.
Sales by food stores were up 0.7 percent to $35.9 billion following a 1.1 percent jump in September.
Gasoline service station sales increased 0.1 percent in October after a 0.4 percent rise in September.
The retail sales report reflects rises in prices as well as volume. Prices for gasoline were higher in October.
